title: Off-Policy Evaluation and Learning for the Future under Non-Stationarity

problem.claim: Estimate and optimize the future value of policies in non-stationary environments using historical data collected by an old policy.

gap.claim: Future-environment data is absent from historical logs, while existing methods assume stationarity or rely on restrictive reward-modeling assumptions that can cause significant bias.

contributions.claim: The OPFV estimator estimates policy values at future time points by using a new type of importance weighting that exploits time-related structure in time-series data.
The paper identifies conditions under which OPFV has low bias.
The estimator is extended into a policy-gradient method for learning a good future policy using only historical data.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe the future off-policy evaluation and learning problem as novel, OPFV's importance weighting as a new type, and their estimator as the first to exploit time-related structures for effective F-OPE.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The methods substantially outperform existing methods for estimating and optimizing future policy value under non-stationarity across various experimental setups.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper formulates future off-policy evaluation and learning for policy values in changing environments.
Future data is unavailable in historical logs, and existing approaches can be biased under non-stationarity.
OPFV uses time-series structure and a new importance-weighting approach to estimate future policy values.
The paper gives low-bias conditions for OPFV and extends it to future policy learning with a policy-gradient method.
The authors report improvements over existing methods across multiple experimental setups.

source_observation.claim: Historical time-series data may contain seasonal, weekly, or holiday structures that also occur in the future environment.

interpretation.claim: Shared temporal structure can provide usable information for future policy evaluation when direct future observations are unavailable.

application.claim: For future-value estimation tasks, model or reweight historical data using temporal patterns that plausibly persist into the target period.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify how persistent the temporal structures must be or how the approach behaves when they change.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the formal assumptions or exact conditions for OPFV's low-bias guarantee.
The abstract does not identify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results used in the experiments.
The abstract does not describe the policy-gradient algorithm's objective or optimization details.
